established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) are actively being applied to NetOps/AIOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, diagnosis, change planning, and limited self-healing) and integrated into multi-agent/agentic frameworks.
limitations: Many records are system descriptions/reports; public quantitative generalization across diverse production networks is limited.

established_findings.statement: Operational reliability of LLM-driven NetOps systems is primarily determined by surrounding engineering (validators, tool-bounds, assurance contracts, sandboxing, rollback mechanisms) rather than by the model alone.
limitations: Argumentative/systematic evidence; limited controlled quantitative comparisons isolating each machinery component's effect size.

established_findings.statement: Generate–validate–repair (or generate–critic) patterns and verifier-in-the-loop architectures are proposed or instantiated to improve correctness of LLM outputs in structured-generation domains and NetOps workflows.
limitations: Some cited instantiations (e.g., PoeTone) are in non-network domains; NetOps instantiations report workflow designs and selected evaluations but not broad benchmarked replication.

established_findings.statement: There exist deterministic/formal network-configuration verification tools and methods (e.g., Minesweeper, formal-methods approaches) that can check rich properties of network configurations and find violations.
limitations: These tools operate on network configuration/route-model abstractions and may have scalability or modeling-coverage limits depending on property and protocol scope.

established_findings.statement: LLM-driven systems exhibit documented failure modes and system-reliability challenges (hallucination/overconfidence, theatrical compliance, loop/stagnation, tool/encoding failures), motivating guardrails and human-in-the-loop oversight.
limitations: Failure-mode studies vary in domain and depth; direct quantitative rates for NetOps-specific misconfiguration from LLMs are limited in the supplied set.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent can LLM-only NetOps systems (without strong deterministic validators and operational guardrails) achieve production-grade correctness and safety across diverse vendor/device families?
limitations: Some systems report production deployments (e.g., Confucius) but the supplied records do not provide comprehensive cross-vendor empirical failure-rate studies that isolate validator presence vs absence.

unresolved_questions.statement: How reliably do LLM-based repair/translation pipelines generalize across heterogeneous real-world device CLIs and evolving vendor syntax?
limitations: INTA reports strong results on particular datasets; broader cross-vendor replication evidence is not present in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What standardized metrics and benchmarks best capture operational safety/reliability (not just task-level accuracy) for agentic NetOps evaluations?
limitations: NetEval and review papers discuss evaluation gaps, but there is no consensus standard provided in the supplied set that operationalizes safety-centric metrics across environments.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is limited publicly documented evidence (in the supplied records) of direct integrations between LLM agents and widely used deterministic network-verification tools (e.g., Batfish) demonstrating end-to-end generate→verify→repair loops.
limitations: Absence here refers to the supplied record set only; other external publications (not supplied) may exist.

candidate_gaps.statement: Construct-valid, operationally realistic NetOps benchmarks that measure safety properties (e.g., rollback success, MTTR under automated changes, false-positive/negative rates of validators when paired with LLM proposals) are underrepresented in the supplied literature.
limitations: Some benchmark efforts (NetEval) and evaluation surveys exist, but they focus on NetOps capability or task accuracy rather than end-to-end operational-safety metrics.

candidate_gaps.statement: Few supplied empirical studies quantify how much surrounding engineering (validators, sandbox replay, canarying, rollback) reduces actual misconfiguration-caused outages when using LLMs.
limitations: System papers argue for these components but do not report controlled ablation-style measurements in the supplied set quantifying outage-reduction effects.

excluded_claims: LLMs by themselves (without validators, sandboxes, or human oversight) are proven safe for production NetOps — excluded due to lack of supporting evidence in the supplied records.

There is strong published evidence in the supplied set that Batfish has been integrated with LLM agents in a published, evaluated end-to-end pipeline — excluded because no supplied record demonstrates this integration.

Any single paper in the supplied set establishes universal superiority of one mitigation (e.g., constrained templates) over others for NetOps safety — excluded because comparative, conclusive results are not present in the supplied records.
